_**Agent (gpt-5.6-luna 2026-08-01 14:19:32Z)**_

Yes—mostly. I’d call it about 80% aligned with Microfilm Dark, with two meaningful corrections.

What tracks:

- Warm OKLCH manila neutrals, never pure white.
- Semantic color rather than decorative accents.
- Hairlines, measured layout, dossier corner clips.
- Typewriter/mono metadata and restrained prose typography.
- Forked readings as the visual thesis; this fits the project’s reading/counter-reading and open-ended research model.
- No side stripes, metric hero blocks, card grids, glow, or generic dashboard chrome.

What needs correction:

1. Typography conflicts with the canonical system.

[DESIGN.md](/Users/liamellis/Desktop/apps/ultraterrestrial-resurrection/DESIGN.md:32) specifies:

- Martian Mono for OCR, metadata, labels, stamps, and badges.
- Special Elite for one wordmark/dossier-title moment.
- Sans for prose.

“Courier New … present everywhere” drifts toward making the typewriter face the system voice. Keep Courier New only if you are intentionally replacing Special Elite, and keep it confined to the single wordmark moment. Otherwise use the existing tokens.

2. “Confirmed damage” is risky terminology.

The design system reserves “confirmed” and “proves” because they can accidentally overstate anomalous conclusions. Use the canonical evidentiary states—`Observed`, `Corroborated`, `Contested`, `Inferred`, `Speculative`, `Resonant`, `Unverified`, `Disconfirmed`—and map damage/degradation/soundness to those states where needed. See [UX_LANGUAGE_GUIDE.md](/Users/liamellis/Desktop/apps/ultraterrestrial-resurrection/docs/vision/UX_LANGUAGE_GUIDE.md:40).

One scope caveat: the light-table theme is compatible with the broader archival-material register, but it is not “Microfilm Dark” itself. Microfilm Dark is explicitly a dark-room canvas where the luminous graph is the subject. If this is a document or synthesis surface, the light theme works. If it is the main research canvas, preserve the dark scene and let the fork topology live inside the graph.

I’d revise the plan to:

> Color: canonical warm OKLCH manila neutrals, never pure white, with the evidentiary palette carrying provenance states semantically. Light mode is a dossier on a light table, not an inversion of the dark canvas. Type: Special Elite or Courier New for one restrained wordmark moment; Martian Mono for OCR, metadata, stamps, and badges; system sans for prose. Layout: a single measured column for document surfaces, hairline-separated, with the forked reading/counter-reading topology as the centerpiece. Use dossier corner clips on major panels. No side stripes, hero metrics, identical card grids, or decorative chrome.

That version tracks the canon cleanly without quietly creating a second design system.

_**Agent (gpt-5.6-luna 2026-08-01 14:37:58Z)**_

Your suspicion is correct. `DESIGN.md` is not a comprehensive design system. It is a narrow, agent-assisted visual contract for one canvas treatment.

Evidence:

- It was introduced in one commit on July 8, 2026: `0ce78d6`.
- The commit was authored by `monichre`, co-authored by “Claude Fable 5.”
- The commit explicitly describes it as a “slight extension of the existing chrome, not a rebuild.”
- The file is only 55 lines and mostly covers palette, typography, texture, motion, and bans.

So it is not the source of truth for the whole product. It is closer to:

> Research Canvas / Microfilm Dark implementation notes

The narrowness is visible in what it omits:

- no light-table or archival-paper register
- no shared document-system rules
- no responsive behavior
- no accessibility or contrast rules
- no spacing, density, sizing, or layout grammar
- no component anatomy
- no distinction between document, evidence, inference, field note, and navigation surfaces
- no rules for when archival-material and techno-analytical registers should combine
- no relationship to the newer document-panel work
- no guidance for the rest of the app

It also overstates a few local choices as universal doctrine:

- “Dark is forced by the scene” only makes sense for the research canvas, not every product surface.
- “Special Elite” and “Martian Mono” are implementation choices, not necessarily the enduring brand typography.
- “Never mix” solid and dashed borders is useful for provenance, but it should apply to source/inference delineation—not become a universal border rule.
- Its bans are good guardrails for avoiding dashboard sludge, but they are not a complete visual language.

The original source material is also internally messy. `RESEARCH_CANVAS_AESTHETIC.md` contains a much louder cyber-noir direction—neon, holograms, scanlines, red string, lens flares—while the newer document-system direction moved toward warm paper, extreme negative space, restrained spot colors, and material evidence. `DESIGN.md` silently picks one branch and calls it canonical.

My blunt verdict: do not throw it away, but demote it. Rename its conceptual role to something like:

> Microfilm Dark — Research Canvas Surface Contract

Then create a higher-level design system above it that defines:

1. the product’s visual thesis;
2. the archival-material and techno-analytical registers;
3. shared document/evidence materiality;
4. typography and color tokens;
5. provenance and epistemic state rules;
6. surface-specific contracts, including Microfilm Dark.

Your proposed plan is actually a better starting point for the document-panel layer than `DESIGN.md` is. The current file should be treated as one branch of the system—not the system itself.

_**Agent (gpt-5.6-luna 2026-08-01 14:39:56Z)**_

Yes—the broader corpus makes the problem much clearer. My previous review gave `DESIGN.md` too much authority.

`DESIGN.md` is a thin extraction from a much larger, messier design world. It captures one narrow branch: the dark research-canvas chrome. It does not represent the breadth of the product’s visual language.

The actual corpus contains at least these layers:

| Corpus | What it covers | What `DESIGN.md` loses |
|---|---|---|
| [00_MASTER_BRAND_BIBLE.md](/Users/liamellis/Desktop/apps/ultraterrestrial-resurrection/docs/design/brand-bible/00_MASTER_BRAND_BIBLE.md) | Product thesis, artifact philosophy, seven visual modes, surfaces, texture, typography roles | Archive Document, Field Evidence, Myth-Tech, Public Release, Dystopian Collage |
| [06_DESIGN_TOKENS.ts](/Users/liamellis/Desktop/apps/ultraterrestrial-resurrection/docs/design/brand-bible/06_DESIGN_TOKENS.ts) | Real token vocabulary, visual modes, archival/digital/texture intensity, polaroid and tape variants | Almost all component-level design logic |
| [Typography README](/Users/liamellis/Desktop/apps/ultraterrestrial-resurrection/apps/app/src/components/design-system/typography/README.md) | Headings, data labels, coordinates, timestamps, handwritten notes, stamps, redaction, glitch, code, body text | Nearly the entire typography behavior system |
| [Typography.md](/Users/liamellis/Desktop/apps/ultraterrestrial-resurrection/apps/app/src/components/design-system/typography/Typography.md) | Actual component API and semantic variants | The idea that typography is a system of expressive roles, not three font assignments |
| [08_PROMPT_LIBRARY](/Users/liamellis/Desktop/apps/ultraterrestrial-resurrection/docs/design/brand-bible/08_PROMPT_LIBRARY/README.md) | Investigative voice, editorial discipline, reusable archive/world-building language | The connection between visual identity and investigative method |
| `docs/design/design-lab/` | Light paper, dossier art, document systems, visual references, storyboards, research-desk compositions | The entire physical/material and light-table direction |

The typography notes alone disprove the idea that the system is simply:

> typewriter wordmark + mono metadata + sans prose

The actual system includes:

- official archival type
- technical mono
- stamped/classification type
- handwritten field notes
- modern AI-war-room UI type
- display headings
- distorted/glitch typography
- redaction and scan-line treatments
- captions, coordinates, timestamps, code, annotations, and evidence labels

That does not mean every historical font or effect should survive. The typography docs are clearly accreted and contain some bad ideas—gradient fire text and endless glitch variants are exactly the kind of visual debt we should prune. But they establish breadth that `DESIGN.md` simply erases.

Your Courier New instinct is also better grounded than I gave it credit for. The brand bible explicitly lists Courier New, Special Elite, OCR-A, JetBrains Mono, and Martian Mono as archival/official typography. The current app even loads a large family of role-specific fonts in [fonts.tsx](/Users/liamellis/Desktop/apps/ultraterrestrial-resurrection/apps/app/src/app/fonts.tsx). The real question is not “Courier New or Special Elite?” It is:

> Which typographic register belongs to which artifact, surface, and epistemic role?

So the correct conclusion is:

`DESIGN.md` should not be the master design system. It should be a local surface contract for one visual mode—probably `noir-research-canvas` / `ai-war-room`.

Your proposed direction is not drifting from the design corpus. It is correcting the false compression introduced by `DESIGN.md`: bringing back the measured document layout, paper/light-table register, real typewriter voice, and evidence-specific topology.

I would not build the whole product to `DESIGN.md`. I would build the document-panel surface to your plan, then define how that surface relates to the broader visual modes.
